headline: World Models are becoming inescapable, powering robots, self-driving cars, and virtual worlds
summary: These AI systems use visual inputs to simulate physics and predict future visual states, creating digital training grounds for everything from home robots to autonomous vehicles.
details: World models, unlike text-based large language models, use visual inputs to generate digital environments that simulate physics. They predict the next visual state of the world from an image, creating 3D generations that look and feel real.

Niantic, the creator of Pokémon Go, has pivoted into world models after selling the game, leveraging its trove of real-world scan data. Their goal is to reconstruct the real world and build detailed replicas.

These software systems are expected to integrate into everyday life, particularly bolstering home robotics and driverless cars by 2027. They provide crucial training grounds for these autonomous systems.

For robots, world models allow practice without physical movement. Users can take photos of a robot's intended environment to generate a 3D model, then run millions of simulations to train the robot on the space's parameters.

Driverless cars also significantly improve using world models. Wayve, for instance, builds generative world models powered by dashcam footage to recreate hazardous roads and unsafe conditions that are impractical to test in real life.
Beyond physical applications, world models are impacting video games, with major players like Tencent investing in their own models due to their core role in physics and 3D rendering.

Large AI companies like Google are advancing their world model capabilities, and investors are funding new ventures. Yann LeCun's Advanced Machines Intelligence startup raised over a billion dollars, and Fei-Fei Li's World Labs was acquired by AMD for over $8 billion.

The rise of world models is also reshaping the labor market by creating new gig work for data collection. People are paid to record videos of their daily activities to help AI labs simulate the physical world.
